item.title: Ask The Person Above You A Question (PART IX): Re: @ Dr Talcite
item.content:encoded:
I'm rather conventional on this - Latin, and perhaps some others:
1. Those with antique writing systems that can hardly be found in today's documentations.
2. Rare, endangered derivations of a bigger language. These are often considered as "dialects", but some of them possesses enough uniqueness that can be standalone linguistically (not specialized in the field, just exemplifying)
Btw I'm already learning some constructed languages that aren't very popular. Esperanto, Lojban for instance (both less than 1 million active speakers NOW by optimistic estimation. Ephermeral existences?). And I can also use Chinese quite fluently :D

item.title: Ask The Person Above You A Question (PART IX): Re: @LiterallyMechanical
item.content:encoded: When I was little, I used to basically tear through a novel a week. As I got older, both my attention span and my general amount of free time nosedived, and I would only read a couple of books in a year. I’m hoping to turn that trend around! Last week I read Gideon the Ninth, an amazing science fantasy book about angsty necromancers, and I just got my hands on the sequel. I highly recommend it!

item.title: Favourite pizza?: Re: Favourite pizza?
item.content:encoded:
If there's nothing else that's interesting, regular cheese pizzas are great (especially when cold). If we're talking about really odd pizzas, though…I once ordered a pizza in Krakow that had broccoli, corn, onions, olive oil, tomatoes, pineapples, and mushrooms on it.

It was fantastic.

item.title: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?: Re: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?
item.content:encoded:
Try SCP-3045, it's got a nice mixture of humor and creepiness. And SCP-2521 is also executed well.
Or just pick a random article and going forward from there.

item.title: Christmas SCPs: Re: Christmas SCPs
item.content:encoded:
SCP-239 apparently created some kind of Santa-like anomaly, though idk if it would continue to exist now that she's in a coma.

If you're interested in Tales, there's a strange number of them featuring Dr. Clef, such as:

  • How Dr. Clef Contained Christmas!
  • How Dr. Clef Saved Christmas
  • How Dr. Clef Got Into My Santa Claus Pants I'll Never Know
  • A Keter Kinda Christmas
  • A Site-19 Christmas Carol is pretty good too, but it's very long.

item.title: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?: Re: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?
item.content:encoded: Well, SCP-3001, SCP-5733 (this is so good), SCP-4001, maybe SCP-1730 is good too, and of the serie I SCP-093, SCP-914 are a good option to read. And the last SCP-4999, good luck reading and i wait that this be useful for you :)

item.title: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?: Re: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?
item.content:encoded: I'm a huge fan of SCP-3000. It's got a good cross between mythology, Lovecraftian horror and tragedy. SCP-1678 gives off a very mysterious and pre-apocalyptic feel. And SCP-426 is just a brilliant idea.

item.title: Christmas SCPs: Christmas SCPs
item.content:encoded:
Hi. I'm looking to do readings (https://www.youtube.com/c/ReadOut) of Christmas SCP items. These are the one's I've got:

784 - Christmas Cheer
1225 - The Worst Christmas
1933 - Bailey's Santa
2497 - Home for the CactusNights
2536 - The Gift That Keeps On Giving
3193 - Christmas War
3355 - St. Nick
4255 - Santa Claus, The Time Traveler
4666 - Yule Man

So, are there any (including deleted ones) that I've missed?
